newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suez to sell SEV stake to Commercial Union.
newsitem.headline: Suez to sell SEV stake to Commercial Union.

text.p: Cie de Suez has agreed to sell 73.1 percent of the capital of Societe d'Epargne Viagere (SEV) to Commercial Union, the two companies said on Thursday.
Commercial Union said in a statement the stake's valuation was around 90 million stg at the end of 1996.

Suez, which has agreed to be taken over by Lyonnaise des Eaux, said in a separate statement that the sale of the SEV stake would contribute positively to 1997 results. A Suez spokesman put the positive impact at "several tens of millions of francs".

"Compagnie de Suez, pursuing chairman Gerard Mestrallet's strategy to focus on core activities, has agreed to the terms of a transaction whereby Commercial Union would acquire its 73.1 percent participation in the capital of Societe d'Epargne Viagere as well as a brokerage specialised in the sale of AFER policies," Suez said in its statement.

Suez and Commercial Union said the deal was agreed with full accordance of the life insurance organisation AFER (Association Francaise d'Epargne et de Retraite) which SEV insures along with Commercial Union subsidiary Abeille Vie.
They said the deal hinged on French and British regulatory approvals.
